clue.text: Misery about border plant

indicators.note: about means going round, so one piece wraps the other here

parts.note: misery means agony
a rim is a border or edge

explanation.surface: Someone is unhappy about a plant growing along the edge of a garden.
explanation.definitionFit: Agrimony is a yellow-flowered herb of the rose family, so it is an example of a plant.

clue.text: Total uniformity nevertheless

definitions.meaning: everything being identical, every one of them alike

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means both 'every one identical' and, as an idiom, 'even so; however'.

clue.text: Letter of protest at songbird

parts.note: round can mean at someone's place, as in 'come round Jo's' meaning at Jo's
the robin is a familiar songbird

explanation.surface: Someone is complaining in writing about a noisy bird.
explanation.walkthrough: The use of 'round' to mean 'at' (someone's house) is informal British speech.
explanation.definitionFit: A round robin is a petition with signatures arranged in a circle, a letter of complaint signed by many.

clue.text: Means of communication enabling me to bring up assistance

indicators.note: in a down clue, bringing up a word means writing it upwards, so read backwards

parts.note: assistance means aid

explanation.surface: Something that lets a person summon help.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to bring up' turns AID into DIA beneath ME.
explanation.definitionFit: The press, television and radio together are the mass channels by which news is communicated.

clue.text: Did this make William the Conqueror successful as a comedian?

definitions.text: Did this make William the Conqueror successful as a comedian?

parts.words: Did this make William the Conqueror successful as a comedian?
parts.note: read literally, the shrewdness of the invaders of 1066 helped William win; it is also the name of a famous British film comedian

explanation.surface: A whimsical historical question about William the Conqueror doing stand-up.
explanation.walkthrough: Norman Wisdom was a hugely popular British slapstick comedian of the 1950s and 60s; the clue also reads as the cleverness of the Normans.
explanation.definitionFit: The name of a well-known British comic actor, also readable as the good sense of the Normans who won at Hastings.

clue.text: A change from the cane

definitions.meaning: a swap or shift from one thing to another
a thin flexible stick used for beating

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a sudden change and a slender rod used to hit someone.

clue.text: Keep quiet about irrigated area between river basins

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one word goes round the other

parts.note: irrigated means watered
sh is the call to keep quiet

explanation.surface: Instructions to stay silent about some well-irrigated land between rivers.
explanation.definitionFit: A watershed is the ridge of high ground dividing two drainage basins.

clue.text: A dynastic spike?

definitions.meaning: a Chinese ruling house, the dynasty of 618 to 907
the pointed prong of a blade that goes into the handle

explanation.definitionFit: Tang is the name of a Chinese dynasty, and also the projecting tongue of a knife blade fixed into the handle.

clue.text: Robin, for instance, on car roof

definitions.meaning: the outlaw of Sherwood Forest is the example
the folding top of a convertible car

explanation.definitionFit: Robin Hood is the legendary outlaw, and a hood is the folding roof of a convertible.

clue.text: Breaks rules and does the washing

definitions.meaning: passing dirty money through clean channels breaks the law

explanation.definitionFit: To launder is to wash clothes, and also to pass illicit money through legitimate channels, an illegal act.

clue.text: Bring back eggs and go for a drink

indicators.note: bring back tells us to write the word for eggs backwards

parts.note: nits are the eggs of lice
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone returns with eggs before heading out for a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Stingo is an old word for a strong ale or beer.

clue.text: Nothing for the wicked? So much the better!

definitions.meaning: read literally, everything goes to the virtuous and none to the bad
an exclamation that an outcome is an improvement

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means a result is beneficial; read literally it says everything goes to good people, leaving none for the wicked.

clue.text: Theatrical character who had large bed prepared

indicators.note: prepared means made ready or put into a new form, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An actor who once owned a big bed that was made up for them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'prepared' rearranges HADLARGEBED. Hedda Gabler is the title heroine of Ibsen's play.
explanation.definitionFit: Hedda Gabler is the title role in Ibsen's 1891 drama, a character from the stage.

clue.text: Take part in discussion of government with police? Is it in order?

definitions.text: Take part in discussion of government

indicators.note: put in order means arranged properly, so the letters are sorted into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A question about whether officers may join a political debate.
explanation.definitionFit: To politicise, in an older intransitive sense, is to engage in political talk or activity.

clue.text: A net closed around one approaching maturity

indicators.note: around signals the letters are moved about into a new order

explanation.surface: A fishing net pulled shut around something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' looks like a container signal, but it rearranges ANETCLOSED.
explanation.definitionFit: An adolescent is a teenager, someone growing towards adulthood.

clue.text: Opening for cat in South Africa

indicators.note: in places one word inside the other

parts.note: a tom is a male cat

explanation.surface: A cat flap in a South African home.
explanation.definitionFit: A stoma is a small mouth-like opening, such as a pore in a leaf or a surgical opening.

clue.text: A number of persons, badly done by, may to very wicked

parts.note: a band is a group of people

indicators.note: badly signals the following word is jumbled

explanation.surface: A group of people who have been treated unfairly might turn bad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'badly' rearranges DONE into ONED. 'by' and 'may to' are link words; the printed 'to' reads like a slip for 'be'.
explanation.definitionFit: Abandoned can mean utterly depraved, lacking all moral restraint.

clue.text: Signal to take care with message

parts.note: watch means be careful, as in 'watch out'
word means news or a message, as in 'send word'

explanation.surface: Advice to be cautious accompanied by a note.
explanation.definitionFit: A watchword is a password or a slogan used as a signal.

clue.text: Might girl's back be her best attribute?

parts.note: main means strength, as in 'with might and main'

indicators.note: back tells us to write the girl's name backwards

parts.note: Tessa is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A cheeky question about whether a woman's behind is her finest feature.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns TESSA into ASSET. 'Might' looks like a verb but is the noun for strength.
explanation.definitionFit: A main asset is someone's chief advantage, the best quality they have.

clue.text: Exercise can be a bore

explanation.definitionFit: A drill is repetitive training, and also a tool for boring holes.

clue.text: Animals seen by learned theologian outside capital sign

indicators.note: outside puts the theologian round the capital

parts.note: DD stands for Doctor of Divinity, a learned theologian's degree
Rome is the Italian capital
Aries is a sign of the zodiac

explanation.surface: Creatures spotted by a scholar of divinity beyond a city's star sign.
explanation.definitionFit: Dromedaries are one-humped camels, examples of animals.

clue.text: Girl bringing boxer to church

parts.note: Muhammad Ali, the famous heavyweight boxer
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A young woman takes a fighter along to a service.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by example: this is a common female first name, as borne by Lewis Carroll's heroine in Wonderland.

clue.text: A minor part of the city

definitions.meaning: a young person under the protection of a guardian or court
an electoral district of a town

explanation.definitionFit: A ward is a minor in someone's care, and also an administrative district of a city.

clue.text: Flower poem by king

parts.note: an ode is a lyric poem
R, from Rex, is the abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: Verses written about a bloom by a monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flower' is crossword shorthand for a river, something that flows; the Oder runs between Germany and Poland.
explanation.definitionFit: The Oder is a river in central Europe, a thing that flows.

clue.text: Forest to start burning

parts.note: the Forest of Arden in Warwickshire, setting of As You Like It

indicators.note: start means take only the opening letter of the word before

explanation.surface: Woodland is about to catch fire.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to start' looks like 'begin to', but 'start' takes the first letter of 'to'.
explanation.definitionFit: Ardent means passionate, fiery, figuratively burning with feeling.

clue.text: Crime: one detectives find in domestic setting

indicators.note: in places the detectives inside the setting

parts.note: home is the domestic setting
I is the Roman numeral for one
CID is the Criminal Investigation Department, British police detectives

explanation.surface: Police investigate a murder committed in a family house.
explanation.definitionFit: Homicide is the killing of a person, a serious crime.

clue.text: Some wilder ideas to laugh at

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.definitionFit: To deride is to mock or ridicule, treat with scorn.

clue.text: Sticking to partisan

definitions.meaning: a follower or supporter of a cause

explanation.definitionFit: Adherent means clinging as an adjective, and as a noun a loyal supporter of a party.
